newsitem.title: BELGIUM: New evidence of Belgian serial killer found.
newsitem.headline: New evidence of Belgian serial killer found.

text.p: The discovery of more body parts near the southern Belgian town of Mons provides further evidence that a serial killer is at work, Mons Public Prosecutor Pierre Honore said on Sunday.
Police found two plastic sacks containing a head, foot and shin on Saturday alongside a road in the village of Havre after being alerted by a passerby, he told Belgian television and radio.
"It's the head of a woman," Honore said. "We can't identify this person."
Police have found at least nine other bags containing the surgically severed body parts of three or four women in the same region since the end of March.
Honore said all the remains were in similar kinds of sacks and were cut up in a similar way.
Police previously said their investigation would focus on recent disappearances of women in Belgium, France and the Netherlands.
They have so far not made any identifications. The remains have been transferred to Liege University hospital where forensic pathologists are attempting to put the puzzle together.
Police have said there was no immediate reason to suspect a link with the killings of five young girls in a paedophile scandal that has rocked the country in the past nine months.
